TEACHER GUIDE · VERSION 1.0

Build a model. Make the thinking visible.

A browser-local K-means studio for an unsupervised-learning summative. Students select features, learn cluster centers, examine results, and defend their decisions.

Start here

Pattern Lab (formerly Cluster Lab) centers only its title in the header, keeps the workspace left-aligned, and provides sun and moon buttons for Light and Dark modes. On the first visit, appearance follows the system preference. Appearance is saved separately from your project and never changes clustering. Existing Cluster Lab project downloads and autosaves remain compatible.

The simplified opening screen offers a sample or CSV upload, followed by a five-row preview. Full data, column details, and writing prompts are expandable. Reflections may be completed entirely in a separate document; no writing is required to train or export.

  1. Open the studio. The 72-song synthetic dataset is ready immediately.
  2. Move through Data → Features → Train → Explore → Model Card.
  3. Save an initial run in Explore. Return to Features or Train, change one setting, refit, and save a second run.
  4. Compare the saved runs. Investigate two new examples and record reasoning.
  5. Complete the model card and export the HTML report. Open the report in a browser and use Print to save a PDF if desired.
  6. Download the complete project as a portable backup. Browser autosave is device/origin-specific, can be cleared, and is not a submission service.
Students supply the interpretations. The app calculates results and preserves evidence; it does not grade students or generate their explanations.

3D views and vocabulary help

In Explore, choose Plot dimensions → 3D. Feature plots need three selected features; PCA uses three principal components. Rotate by dragging or using arrow keys, adjust zoom, or select Reset view. t-SNE computes a separate 3D embedding and retains both 2D and 3D results. Changing the view never changes the fitted clusters. A third dimension can reveal overlap hidden by a flat view, but is not evidence that groups are natural categories. Use the numbered cluster summaries alongside the plot.

Question-mark buttons open short definitions, including inertia, silhouette, centroids, scaling, PCA, and t-SNE settings. The model card documents purpose, settings, evidence, and limitations. Its writing fields are optional when students use a separate assessment document.

A 25-minute first investigation

  1. 0–4 minutes: inspect the song features. State a useful grouping question.
  2. 4–8: select numerical features, justify the choices, and leave scaling on.
  3. 8–12: use K=3. Watch initial centers, assignment, and center updates; then fit the model.
  4. 12–17: interpret and name groups with evidence. Save the run. Predict the effect of changing K to 4; refit and save.
  5. 17–22: compare member records and means. Assign a typical and an unusual new example.
  6. 22–25: record a limitation and explain what you chose versus what the algorithm learned.

For a summative, allow additional time for original data, peer feedback, model documentation, and a short demonstration. Students who have studied dimensionality reduction can compare PCA and t-SNE and explain why their layouts differ.

Do not reward the highest silhouette, lowest inertia, or a particular grouping. Different defensible designs can demonstrate strong understanding. Use the individual reflection to check every group member’s understanding.

Samples and source

Singapore air quality — download CSV: 500 Central-region observations from 1–22 January 2024, published by NEA via data.gov.sg. Five pollutant measurements retain their averaging periods. There are 17 missing cells; dropping incomplete rows leaves 492 examples. This short historical sample is for exploring patterns, not predicting PSI bands or making health decisions.

Dataset provenance, licenses, and classroom transformations. Penguin measurements suit discussions of similarities and feature scales; historical car data supports investigation of transport trade-offs. Neither dataset supplies correct categories for grading.

Three real datasets are bundled locally with documented attribution and missing values. The original six synthetic datasets remain available, generated with seed 614. There are no hidden group labels used in fitting.

  • Penguin field study — 344 records, four body measurements; 342 complete rows; CC0. Species labels omitted.
  • Cars & fuel use — 398 historical vehicle records, five measurements; 392 complete rows; CC BY 4.0. Origin codes omitted.
  • Fictional songs — BPM and illustrative 0–1 audio features
  • Objects — length/width in cm, mass in grams
  • Separated groups
  • Overlapping groups
  • Continuous variation
  • Curved groups

Download source, tests, and static application. The application files in dist/ can be served by a normal static web host over HTTPS or localhost. Opening index.html with a file:// URL is not supported because module workers require a web origin.

The app itself has no login, paid API, telemetry, remote data processing, or runtime CDN dependency. Site access is controlled separately from the app. Only viewers allowed by the current sharing settings can open the hosted version.

Mathematical implementation

Preprocessing: missing cells are either removed or filled with a feature mean. Scaling uses population standard deviation (denominator n). Values are fitted once and reused. Constant columns are excluded; at least two nonconstant features must remain. Numeric values are bounded to ±10¹² for numerical safety.

K-means: seeded Mulberry32 randomness, K-means++ initialization, 10 initializations by default, 300 update limit. K is limited to 1–12 and the distinct-row count. Exact distance ties choose the first center. Empty clusters receive the farthest eligible point from a group with more than one member. Means are recalculated afterward. A converged result requires unchanged nearest-center assignments after mean updates. Nonconverged runs are explicitly identified. Ordinary fitting prioritizes converged runs and chooses the lowest inertia among them.

Silhouette: exact all-pairs Euclidean distances in fitted space, without sampling, for up to 500 examples. Singleton score 0; zero denominator score 0; undefined if occupied groups are fewer than 2 or equal the sample count. It measures cohesion/separation, not correctness.

PCA: centered covariance matrix with symmetric Jacobi eigendecomposition; components sorted by descending eigenvalue. Pairwise projected distances and explained variance are checked against scikit-learn. Centers share the same transform. Component signs are arbitrary.

t-SNE: upstream Andrej Karpathy tSNEJS, bundled unchanged and pinned by SHA-256: 70a7d6cd823fdc707c91b7cfa0036cd59a2199de6d5b7af9bb1f1081325a77f1. Two or three dimensions (computed separately), default perplexity 20, 500 iterations, learning rate 10, seed 42. The worker supplies seeded Math.random before initializing the library. Same settings reproduce coordinates in the tested runtime; cross-engine floating-point variation is possible. Workers can be terminated to cancel calculation. No centers or new-example transforms are invented for t-SNE.

t-SNE coordinate tests confirm finite deterministic results and worker operation, not universal scientific validity for every dataset. It is a nonconvex visualization and must be interpreted cautiously.

All grouping and quality metrics use the complete selected feature space. Plot changes do not change assignments. Inertia cannot be compared directly across different data or transformations.

Verification and limitations

Read the actual test report for expected and observed outcomes.

Passed: 17 numerical/data checks, 16 DOM interaction checks, 4 actual worker-code checks, 10 additional 3D/definition checks, 8 real-data/theme checks, and 2 NEA source/fitting checks. The fixture centers are (0,1) and (10,11), inertia 4. References use scikit-learn 1.8.0. DOM checks use jsdom 26.1.0; worker checks use Node worker_threads with a Web Worker message bridge.

Browser checks, 26 October 2026: the new NEA sample loaded in cloud Chrome, feature preparation showed 492 complete examples, and K=3 converged after 7 updates with inertia 1,408.266. Light and dark desktop appearance inspected. Other checks remain limited: Tablet layouts, browser-specific downloads, print layout, and keyboard/screen-reader behavior remain unverified. DOM tests are not a substitute for these checks. Pilot the application before using it for a graded assessment.

Limits: 500 rows, 25 columns, 2 MB CSV; 20 saved runs; 15 MB project import. Only numerical clustering features are supported. Uploaded features show “units not supplied”; students should document units in their dataset notes. Unknown category columns need to be excluded by students even if encoded as numbers. Autosave can fail if storage is unavailable or full; use project downloads.

Desktop light and dark appearance has been inspected in cloud Chrome. Tablet layout and full accessibility testing remain outstanding. Dataset examples can be used without completing every reflection, and exports may be drafts. No automatic grading or LMS submission is included.
